payload.name: PreserveExplicitAttributedValuesSeparately
payload.description: When a message explicitly attributes a value, lesson, or advice to a specific person and the speaker indicates a future intention to follow it, extract that as its own focused memory instead of folding it into a broad conversation summary.
content: During extraction, if a message explicitly states that a specific person stressed or taught a value and the speaker says they want to keep it in mind, create a separate memory capturing that specific value and the person who stressed it, rather than only creating a broad event summary of the conversation.

Before merging into an existing general memory, check that this explicit value/attribution is preserved as its own claim; if the existing memory lacks it, add or update a dedicated memory with the specific value and the person who stressed it.

solves: Construction fails when a message contains an explicit attribution of a value/lesson to a specific person plus the speaker's stated intent to apply it, because one broad conversation summary omits that durable claim. This rule applies during extraction/CRUD whenever such explicit attributed values occur; it does not apply to general conversation summaries with no explicit attribution.
